To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
transplantation of fat body cells from one larva to another, leads to the induction of ultrastructural precocious changes in the transplants.
transplantation of fragments of the fat body of one Calliphora larva to another induces ultrastructural changes in cells of fat body transplants.

the transplantation of a fragment of the anterior fat-body lobe of 3- to 4-day-old Calliphora larvae into one-day-older larvae induces precocious metamorphic changes in the transplants and that the extent of the changes induced is influenced by the host's physiological condition at the time of the operation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the fat body of the blowfly, Calliphora erythrocephala.
the question of whether the physiological state of a host can influence the ultrastructure of transplants of larval cells.

the question as to whether the fat body cells of the blowfly, Calliphora erythrocephala, are capable of responding to environmental signals in a manner similar to that observed in cells of vertebrates and invertebrates, such as the amphibian tail, the salivary gland of the blowfly and the wing disc of the fruit fly.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

(1) the fat body of larvae is a heterogeneous tissue; (2) the fat body cells of larvae can undergo premetamorphic ultrastructural changes in response to the physiological environment of the host; (3) the fat body can be used as an experimental model system for studies on the regulation of cellular metabolism in a tissue of a holometabolous insect.
the fat body is an endocrine organ which is capable of responding to the internal environment of the host.

(a) the fat body of the Calliphora larva is a highly plastic tissue which is capable of undergoing a series of ultrastructural changes, which are characteristic of the physiological state of the animal, and (b) the fat body is an important organ for the control and regulation of the physiological state in the Calliphora larvae.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fat body cells are capable of responding to the internal environment of the insect and are therefore sensitive indicators of physiological condition.
the fat body is the target organ for physiological signals which initiate metamorphosis.
the fat body of the larval stage of Calliphora is a dynamic organ, which is able to respond to physiological changes in its environment by the induction of ultrastructural alterations in its cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can induce precocious metamorphosis in the fat body of the blow fly Calliphora vicina by transplantation of fat body fragments from one larva into a host that is at the end of the feeding stage.
the fat body is a useful model for investigating cellular changes induced by physiological conditions during the metamorphic period of insect development.
the fat body of the larva is an important site of the physiological and biochemical changes that occur in the larva at the end of the feeding stage.
